todays_decisions.reasoning: I agree with the Market Analyst's neutral stance: the trend filter passes (SPY 5.6% above its 200-day) but tech is being sold, leadership is defensive, and the Fed meets next week after a hot PPI. Cash is 32% of equity and the owner wants to be mostly invested within about a week, so I deploy part of it now and stage the rest rather than rush to 90% in one day. I approve VRSN at a smaller size, BND as the single bond holding, and a small VOO add. I reject MTCH and IEF. MTCH is a Technology name the Market Analyst says to avoid, and the Skeptic's point that the proposer cited tech weakness as a reason to size down (rather than to skip) stands. IEF duplicates BND (the Implicator counts the pair as one $50 rate bet ahead of the Fed). Approved buys total $70, which leaves about $125 (21%) in cash. That is still above the target, but I would rather add over the coming days once the Fed meeting and VRSN's post-print reaction are visible. L1 shaped the VRSN invalidation, which is anchored to the actual fill. L2 was followed: earnings dates for VRSN (reported 10-22), BND and VOO were checked in the news note.

trades.thesis: Fundamentals rank #1 (only 9/9 F-score, CFO $1.09B vs net income $826M). The Q3 print on 10-22 is out (small EPS miss, small revenue beat, FY26 sales guide raised), so the event risk is gone. Beta 0.03 suits a tech sell-off. Cut from $35 to $25 because the Skeptic is right that the post-print price reaction is not visible in the inputs and a single-stock gap is not captured by beta.
trades.invalidation: Review or exit if it closes more than 10% below the actual fill price (set the level from the fill, not the 10-20 menu close of $306.48, per L1), or if a follow-on 8-K or guidance change shows the 10-22 revenue guide was misread.

trades.thesis: The account holds no bonds and bonds are the one sleeve rallying (+1.13% over 21 days, 4% vol). BND diversifies against the equity-heavy book and the tech sell-off. It is not a short-duration fund, and the rally is reversible around next week's Fed meeting, so it is held as the only bond holding at a modest size. The Skeptic's duplicate objection is met by rejecting IEF.
trades.invalidation: Sell if BND closes more than 2% below the fill price, or if a hawkish Fed pushes the 10-year back above 5.15%.

trades.thesis: The regime is on and breadth is healthy (RSP +3.27% over 21 days), so the Market Analyst prefers broad US exposure over QQQ. Cut from $25 to $15 because the Skeptic and Implicator are right that this mostly duplicates VTI and the Implicator's added-stress figure puts VOO first, with little new exposure. At $15 VOO ends near 12% of equity, well inside the 15% cap. It keeps some core equity exposure while cash is high without leaning on a cash-parking argument.
trades.invalidation: Sell if SPY closes below its 200-day (about 723.62), or if QQQ loses its 200-day and the weakness spreads to the broad index.

rejected.why: MTCH is labelled Technology, the sector the Market Analyst puts on its avoid list. It is ranked 6th with the lowest in-sector percentile of the top group. It reports about 11-03 on an approximate date, and a 10% invalidation can be breached by one earnings gap on a 0.887-beta name. The only catalyst is a 3-day-old upgrade. It also pushes Technology from 5.2% to 15.1% of equity, which the Implicator flagged. The Skeptic's case outweighs the cash-deployment argument.

IEF is a near-duplicate of BND (betas 0.123 vs 0.121). The Skeptic and Implicator both note that BND plus IEF is one $50 rate bet going into next week's Fed meeting after a hot PPI. The Market Analyst recommended BND or IEF, not both. I keep BND and drop IEF.

DPZ.thesis: High-quality, cash-backed franchisor (F-score 8/9, cfo $792M vs net income $602M, gross profitability 1.15) with a 252d beta of 0.095 (-$0.62 on this position in a 10% market drop). That makes it a genuinely defensive starter position while the tape rotates away from tech. Its top-of-sector rank is partly an artifact of the wholesale-groceries mislabel, so the case rests on its absolute quality and low beta, not on the Staples tilt. No earnings inside 5 trading days.
DPZ.invalidation: DPZ closes below $274.88 (10% under the $305.42 reference close), or a fundamentals screen (including one that reflects the Q3 results reported 10-13) drops it from the menu or shows cfo below net income.

IDXX.thesis: Quality Health Care name in a favored sector (F-score 8/9, gp_sector_pct 0.941, cfo $1,182M vs net income $1,059M, no added leverage or dilution). Sized down to $40 because its 0.814 beta (-$3.26 on this position in a 10% drop) makes it the least defensive holding in the book. Earnings are estimated for 11-02, outside the 5-day window.
IDXX.invalidation: IDXX closes below $500.22 (10% under the $555.80 reference close), or IDXX underperforms XLV by more than 5 percentage points over a 21-trading-day window.

WMT.thesis: Low-volatility defensive exposure (vol 0.263, beta about zero; not a hedge) in a favored sector (XLP +6.02% 21d), with positive sell-side sentiment and no earnings until ~11-19. Fundamentals pass the screen (F-score 7, gp_sector_pct 0.865) with no red flags. Sized below the proposal because the staples move has already run and today's upgrades may be priced in, and because it lifts the Consumer Staples label to about 22.5% of equity alongside DPZ.
WMT.invalidation: WMT closes more than 7% below entry, or XLP gives back half its 21-day gain (21-day return below ~+3%) while SPY holds, or WMT cuts guidance at its ~11-19 report.

VTI.thesis: Broad-market exposure to deploy idle cash while the trend is intact and breadth is improving. The Skeptic and Implicator note it largely duplicates VOO and raises beta, and that small caps are weak, so I buy a smaller tranche and hold back the rest given the risk-off open. Resulting US broad-ETF weight is about 18.4%.
VTI.invalidation: SPY closes below its 200-day SMA (723.23), or the position is down more than 8% from the actual fill.

FAST.thesis: Lowest volatility on the menu (0.243), F-score 8/9, gross profitability at the 89th sector percentile, and operating cash flow above net income. It adds a first Consumer Discretionary exposure, not overlapping the staples names held. Resized from $40: the Skeptic is right that its earnings date was never verified, that cash conversion is only about 1.03x, and that the sector label may flatter it. The Implicator confirmed the diversification claim holds.
FAST.invalidation: A close more than 10% below the actual fill price, or an earnings report showing operating cash flow clearly below net income.

CARG.thesis: Rank 2 on fundamentals (gross profitability 1.27, cfo about 2x net income), earnings 11-05 are outside the 5-day window, and no adverse headlines. The Skeptic's objections (averaging a one-day-old position, Technology label against the sector view, vol near the cutoff) justify a small add: the combined position is about 5%, and I will judge it as one position.
CARG.invalidation: Combined position closes more than 10% below the average fill (measured from actual fills, per L1), or a negative earnings surprise appears inside the next five trading days.

BTC/USD.thesis: A small crypto slot: trend still positive (63-day +28%, 14% above its 200-day), ETF inflows recovering, and no exchange failures or new adverse regulatory action. Resized from $20: the Skeptic is right that the thesis is mostly diversification, volatility is 44%, and the recovery partly rides on the same Iran-deal headline as energy. The Implicator's stress test shows this is the highest-risk sleeve per dollar.
BTC/USD.invalidation: A close more than 10% below the actual fill price, or an exchange failure or adverse regulatory action appears in the news.

KR.thesis: Staples is a Market Analyst favored sector, KR has low event risk (next earnings 12-03, the 10-20 8-K was an investor-day update) and the sell side is supportive after the 7-11% EPS CAGR target. The Skeptic and Implicator are right that this stacks on WMT and DPZ (staples about 22.5% of equity) and that the negative beta is a statistical artifact, so I take a smaller position, which lifts staples only to about 25.9%.
KR.invalidation: Close more than 8% below the actual fill price, or the 10-17 grocery-chain cyber incident is confirmed to be Kroger, or a guidance cut at the 12-03 print.

MSCI.thesis: Clean Q3 beat with the earnings event passed (the issue that sank it on 10-20), F-score 8, cfo $1.59B vs net income $1.20B, beta 0.34, and it adds a sector the book does not hold. The Skeptic is right that the sector label is Industrials (not a favored sector) and that the post-print re-rating is partly priced, so I trim the size and rest the case on quality and diversification only.
MSCI.invalidation: Close more than 8% below the actual fill price (anchored to the fill, not the pre-print 563.49 close, per L1), or a guidance cut or negative 8-K follow-up.
